data.name: Overview_Subtitle
data.value: Live status of the HADA service, its connections and entities.

data.name: Update_Detail
data.value: The installer is downloaded from GitHub, checked against its published checksum and started. Your settings are kept.

data.name: Update_DetailElevated
data.value: To install it, use the HADA window opened from the tray icon, not this administrator window.

data.name: Update_DetailPortable
data.value: This is a portable copy: download the portable ZIP of the new version, exit HADA, and replace the service and tray folders. Keep the data folder; it holds your settings.

data.name: Update_Started
data.value: The installer was started; carry on in its window. HADA closes while it is being replaced.

data.name: Update_Failed
data.value: The download did not work: {0} You can also get the installer from the release page.

data.name: Update_UpToDate
data.value: This is the newest version. Checked {0:g}.

data.name: Update_Hidden
data.value: There is nothing to compare with: GitHub does not show HADA's releases without signing in, which is so while the repository is private. Checked {0:g}.

data.name: Preferences_Subtitle
data.value: Updates, and how HADA behaves for you on this computer.

data.name: Preferences_AutoCheckDetail
data.value: Once a day the service asks GitHub whether a newer version was released. Nothing is downloaded until you ask for it.

data.name: Preferences_PrereleasesDetail
data.value: Versions marked as pre-release: they have the newest features, and have been tried less.

data.name: Preferences_LockedMessage
data.value: Changing how updates are checked requires administrator rights. Checking now, and your personal settings below, do not.

data.name: Preferences_PersonalDetail
data.value: These apply to your account only, take effect at once and need no administrator rights.

data.name: Preferences_PersonalElevated
data.value: These are your personal settings. Change them in the HADA window opened from the tray icon, not in this administrator window.

data.name: Preferences_LanguageDetail
data.value: Of this window and the tray icon's menu.

data.name: Preferences_LanguageRestart
data.value: The window shows the new language when it is opened again; the tray icon's menu after the tray app is restarted.

data.name: Preferences_IdleDetail
data.value: How many seconds after the last keyboard or mouse input the "User active" sensor turns off.

data.name: Preferences_DashboardDetail
data.value: A small window opened from the tray icon's menu. Each Home Assistant that HADA connects to directly has its dashboard here: switch off the ones you do not want, or give an address of your own, a particular dashboard for instance.

data.name: Dashboard_Failed
data.value:
The dashboard cannot be shown: {0}
It needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 11 includes and Windows 10 may lack.

data.name: Autostart_Detail
data.value: Starts the tray app, and with it the session sensors and controls, when you sign in. The HADA service always starts with Windows.

data.name: Autostart_DetailPortable
data.value: Starts this portable copy of HADA when you sign in, by adding it to your startup programs. Turn it off before you move or delete the folder.

data.name: Status_NotRunningDetail
data.value: Start the HADA service to see live data.

data.name: State_NotConfiguredDetail
data.value: Set it up on the Connections page.

data.name: Tray_ClientsDetail
data.value: Sensors and controls of your desktop (windows, sound, media, display, notifications) come from the tray app.

data.name: Entity_Unavailable
data.value: Unavailable – the tray app is not running, or another user is at the computer

data.name: Connections_Subtitle
data.value: How HADA talks to Home Assistant: through MQTT or directly, either way to one Home Assistant or several at once.

data.name: Mqtt_Description
data.value: For those who have an MQTT broker. Everything appears in Home Assistant by itself, with buttons and switches to click.

data.name: Ha_Description
data.value: Direct connection, without a broker. What it gives depends on Entities below.

data.name: Placeholder_SecretSaved
data.value: Saved – leave empty to keep it

data.name: Validation_Host
data.value: The broker host is not a valid host name or IP address.

data.name: Validation_Port
data.value: The port must be a whole number between 1 and 65535.

data.name: Validation_Topic
data.value: Topic prefixes must not be empty or contain spaces, + or #.

data.name: Validation_UrlRequired
data.value: Enter the Home Assistant URL first.

data.name: Validation_Url
data.value: The Home Assistant URL must start with http:// or https://.

data.name: Validation_EventType
data.value: The command event type must not be empty or contain spaces.

data.name: Validation_CustomName
data.value: Custom entities: every entry needs a name.

data.name: Validation_CustomValue
data.value: Custom entities: "{0}" has no value, process name, command, program or keys.

data.name: Error_ServiceUnavailable
data.value: The HADA service is not running or cannot be reached.

data.name: Entities_Subtitle
data.value: Choose what this computer shares with Home Assistant, and what Home Assistant may do to it. Disabled entities are removed from Home Assistant. The buttons that switch the computer off are off until you turn them on.

data.name: Entities_Empty
data.value: No entities are registered yet. Is the HADA service running?

data.name: EntityHint_active_window
data.value: Sends window titles, which can contain document names, e-mail subjects or web page titles.

data.name: EntityHint_lock_screen
data.value: Lets Home Assistant lock this computer.

data.name: EntityHint_display_on
data.value: On while the screen is on, including when it is dimmed.

data.name: EntityHint_session_locked
data.value: On while Windows is locked or showing the sign-in screen.

data.name: EntityHint_user_active
data.value: On when the keyboard or mouse was used lately: within the last minute, or the time you set on the Settings page.

data.name: EntityHint_microphone_in_use
data.value: On while an app is using the microphone. The app names are sent as an attribute.

data.name: EntityHint_microphone_muted
data.value: On while the microphone is muted in Windows. Muting inside a call app only is not seen.

data.name: EntityHint_external_display
data.value: On while a monitor other than the built-in one is connected. A monitor without power is not seen; to know whether the computer is docked, add a "Device is connected" custom sensor for the dock.

data.name: EntityHint_camera_in_use
data.value: On while an app is using the camera. The app names are sent as an attribute.

data.name: EntityHint_active_user
data.value: The account name of whoever is signed in at this computer; "none" on the sign-in screen.

data.name: EntityHint_ip_address
data.value: The address of the connection Windows routes through. Its name and type are attributes.

data.name: EntityHint_wifi_network
data.value: The name of the connected Wi-Fi network, with the signal strength as an attribute. Recent versions of Windows hide the name unless location access is allowed.

data.name: EntityHint_disk_usage
data.value: How full the drive is. Free and total space are attributes.

data.name: EntityHint_audio_device
data.value: The name of the default playback device, so an automation can tell headphones from speakers. The default microphone is an attribute.

data.name: EntityHint_do_not_disturb
data.value: On while Windows holds notifications back (Do not disturb).

data.name: EntityHint_media_playback
data.value: Whether media is playing. Sends the title, artist, album and app as attributes.

data.name: EntityHint_update_available
data.value: On when a newer HADA was released. The service asks GitHub once a day, unless that is turned off on the Settings page.

data.name: EntityHint_gpu_load
data.value: How busy the graphics processor is, as Task Manager shows it.

data.name: EntityHint_sleep
data.value: Lets Home Assistant put this computer to sleep. Off until you turn it on.

data.name: EntityHint_hibernate
data.value: Lets Home Assistant hibernate this computer. Off until you turn it on.

data.name: EntityHint_shutdown
data.value: Lets Home Assistant shut this computer down. Apps with unsaved work can still object. Off until you turn it on.

data.name: EntityHint_restart
data.value: Lets Home Assistant restart this computer. Apps with unsaved work can still object. Off until you turn it on.

data.name: EntityHint_turn_off_display
data.value: Lets Home Assistant turn the screen off. Many laptops go to sleep soon after.

data.name: EntityHint_wake_display
data.value: Lets Home Assistant turn the screen back on, as moving the mouse would. Cannot wake a computer that is asleep.

data.name: EntityHint_media_play_pause
data.value: Presses the play/pause key; whichever app handles media keys reacts.

data.name: EntityHint_volume_level
data.value: Lets Home Assistant set the volume of the default playback device.

data.name: EntityHint_audio_mute
data.value: Lets Home Assistant mute and unmute the default playback device.

data.name: EntityHint_microphone_mute
data.value: Lets Home Assistant mute and unmute the default microphone in Windows.

data.name: EntityHint_notification
data.value: Messages sent to this entity are shown as Windows notifications, with a picture and buttons if the message has them.

data.name: Custom_Title
data.value: Custom sensors, buttons and quick actions

data.name: Custom_Subtitle
data.value: Your own sensors: a fixed text, whether a program is running or a device is connected, the result of a PowerShell command. Your own buttons for Home Assistant to press: run a command, start a program, press keys. And quick actions: entries in the tray icon's menu, optionally with a keyboard shortcut, that start an automation in Home Assistant.

data.name: Custom_Empty
data.value: Nothing here yet. Add a sensor to send your own value to Home Assistant, a button for Home Assistant to press, or a quick action to start an automation from this computer.

data.name: Custom_ValueCommandButton
data.value: Command – run when the button is pressed

data.name: Custom_ValueLaunchButton
data.value: Program, document or address to open

data.name: Custom_ValueDevice
data.value: Device ID, or a part of it

data.name: Custom_DevicePicker
data.value: Or pick a connected USB device

data.name: Custom_ValuePowerShell
data.value: Command – its output becomes the value

data.name: Custom_PowerShellNote
data.value: PowerShell commands, of sensors and of buttons, are run by the HADA service with system rights, not as you, so they cannot see your desktop or your user's files and settings. A sensor's command that fails or takes longer than 30 seconds is reported on the Logs page; a button's command may take up to 10 minutes.

data.name: Custom_ButtonNote
data.value: A program a button starts runs on the desktop of whoever is signed in, with that user's rights, so the tray app must be running. Put a path that contains spaces in quotes.

data.name: Custom_QuickActionNote
data.value: A quick action does nothing on this computer by itself. It appears in the tray icon's menu and as a trigger of this device in Home Assistant; build an automation on that trigger to say what it does.

data.name: Logs_Subtitle
data.value: Recent messages from the HADA service.

data.name: Mqtt_OneServer
data.value: To report to several Home Assistants at once, e.g. one in each place, add a server for each.

data.name: Mqtt_ServerNameHint
data.value: Your name for this Home Assistant, shown here and in the logs. Needed once there are several.

data.name: Validation_ServerName
data.value: Give each MQTT server a name, to tell them apart.

data.name: Preferences_BrowserDetail
data.value: Where the address of a notification, or of one of its buttons, is opened when you press it.

data.name: Ha_NotificationsHint
data.value: Registers this computer in Home Assistant the way a phone is. Home Assistant then has the action notify.mobile_app_ followed by the device name, with a title, a picture and buttons. With the HADA integration this is not needed: it has an action of its own, hada.notify.

data.name: Issue_integration_missing
data.value: The HADA integration is not installed in this Home Assistant, so the entities are not there. Install it with HACS, or choose another way for the sensors.

data.name: Issue_integration_not_set_up
data.value: The HADA integration is installed but not set up. In Home Assistant, go to Settings, Devices and services, Add integration, and choose HADA.

data.name: Issue_integration_unauthorized
data.value: Another Home Assistant user connected this Device ID first. Use that user's token or an administrator's, or another Device ID.

data.name: Issue_integration_unsupported
data.value: The HADA integration in this Home Assistant is too new for this version of HADA. Update HADA.

data.name: Issue_integration_failed
data.value: The HADA integration did not accept the computer. See the logs here and in Home Assistant.

data.name: Issue_other
data.value: Something keeps this connection from doing all it should: {0}.

data.name: Validation_HaServerName
data.value: Give each Home Assistant server a name, to tell them apart.

data.name: Validation_HaServerNameTwice
data.value: Two Home Assistant servers are called "{0}".

data.name: Guide_Intro
data.value: There are three ways to connect HADA to Home Assistant. You can use more than one, as long as the entities go through only one of them.

data.name: Guide_MqttText
data.value: For those who have an MQTT broker, for example Mosquitto. Gives everything: sensors, and buttons, switches and sliders to click in Home Assistant. Nothing to install in Home Assistant.

data.name: Guide_DirectText
data.value: Needs only the address of Home Assistant and an access token. Gives sensors, and notifications as on a phone, with pictures and buttons. There are no buttons or switches for the computer to click in Home Assistant. Below, set Entities to "As entities of the device".

data.name: Guide_IntegrationTitle
data.value: Direct connection with the HADA integration

data.name: Guide_IntegrationText
data.value: Gives everything, as MQTT does, without a broker. The HADA integration has to be installed in Home Assistant first, with HACS. Below, set Entities to "Through the HADA integration".

data.name: Guide_Mix
data.value: A common mix: MQTT for the entities, and a direct connection with Entities set to "Off", only for notifications with pictures from cameras.

data.name: Ha_SensorsDetail_Off
data.value: Nothing is sent through this connection. Choose this when this Home Assistant gets the entities through MQTT.

data.name: Ha_SensorsDetail_Entities
data.value: Sensors only, with nothing to install. The computer appears in Home Assistant under Mobile App. There are no buttons or switches to click there.

data.name: Ha_SensorsDetail_Integration
data.value: Sensors, buttons, switches and sliders, as with MQTT. Needs the HADA integration installed in Home Assistant, with HACS; while it is missing, the Overview page says so.

data.name: Ha_SensorsDetail_States
data.value: The earlier way: sensors only, forgotten when Home Assistant restarts, and it needs an administrator’s token. Kept for connections set up before there was a choice.

data.name: Ha_UrlEncrypted
data.value: Encrypted: nobody on the way can read the access token or what is sent.

data.name: Ha_UrlUnencryptedLocal
data.value: Not encrypted. Fine on your own network; from outside it, use an https:// address.

data.name: Ha_UrlUnencryptedPublic
data.value: Not encrypted, and this reads like an address on the internet: the access token could be read on the way. HADA does not connect to such an address. Use https://, or allow it below if you are sure.

data.name: Ha_UrlUnencryptedAllowed
data.value: Not encrypted, and allowed all the same: the access token can be read on the way to this address.

data.name: Ha_AllowUnencrypted
data.value: Connect to this address without encryption

data.name: Issue_unencrypted_public
data.value: HADA did not connect: the address is not encrypted (http) and is a public one, so the access token would travel in the open. Use an https:// address, or allow the unencrypted connection for this server on the Connections page.

data.name: Issue_integration_outdated
data.value: The HADA integration in this Home Assistant is older than this version of HADA, and left some entities out. Update it in Home Assistant, with HACS, and restart Home Assistant.

data.name: Preferences_DashboardOtherDetail
data.value: For a Home Assistant connected through MQTT, or any other page. Leave empty if you do not need it.

data.name: Ha_HomeTitle
data.value: Another address on your home network

data.name: Ha_HomeIntro
data.value: While the computer is on one of the networks named here, HADA connects to Home Assistant at this address, without going out to the internet and back. Everywhere else it uses the address above, and so it does when the local one does not answer.

data.name: Ha_ConnectedNetworks
data.value: Connected now, by the names Windows knows them by. Click one to add it:

data.name: Ha_HomeNoNetworks
data.value: Name at least one home network: without one the local address is never used.

data.name: Ha_HomeNoAddress
data.value: Enter the address Home Assistant has on these networks.

data.name: Validation_LocalUrl
data.value: The address on the home network must be a full http:// or https:// address.

data.name: Reach_Title
data.value: Not everything below reaches Home Assistant

data.name: Reach_Entities
data.value: sensors arrive as entities of the device. Buttons, switches and sliders cannot be clicked in Home Assistant through this connection; choose "Through the HADA integration" for it on the Connections page, or use MQTT.

data.name: Reach_States
data.value: the earlier way: sensors only, as states that Home Assistant forgets when it restarts. Buttons, switches and sliders cannot be clicked there; choose "Through the HADA integration" for this connection on the Connections page, or use MQTT.

data.name: Reach_NotificationsOnly
data.value: notifications only. No entities are sent through this connection, and there is no other.

data.name: Reach_Nothing
data.value: nothing is sent through this connection: its entities and its notifications are both switched off.

data.name: Reach_NoConnection
data.value: HADA is not connected to any Home Assistant yet. Set one up on the Connections page.

data.name: EntityHint_media_player
data.value: Playback, volume and what is playing as one entity, as Home Assistant shows a speaker. Only through the HADA integration; the separate media buttons, the volume slider and the playback sensor work every way.

data.name: Reach_MediaPlayer
data.value: appears in Home Assistant only through the HADA integration, which none of your connections uses. The media buttons, the volume slider and the playback sensor arrive as before.

data.name: EntityHint_restart_required
data.value: On while Windows waits for a restart to finish installing updates.

data.name: EntityHint_screen_brightness
data.value: The brightness of the built-in screen, which Home Assistant can also set. Only on computers with a screen Windows can dim.

data.name: SignIn_Hint
data.value: Instead of a token: opens Home Assistant in your browser, where you sign in and allow the access.

data.name: SignIn_Waiting
data.value: Waiting for you to sign in in the browser…

data.name: SignIn_Done
data.value: Signed in. Save to start using it.

data.name: SignIn_NeedsAddress
data.value: Enter the address of Home Assistant first.

data.name: SignIn_Unencrypted
data.value: Signing in needs an encrypted address (https://), or your leave for this one under the address.

data.name: SignIn_TimedOut
data.value: Nobody signed in within five minutes. Try again.

data.name: SignIn_BrowserClose
data.value: You can close this tab and go back to HADA.

data.name: Placeholder_SignedIn
data.value: Signed in through Home Assistant – leave empty to keep

data.name: Issue_sign_in_expired
data.value: Home Assistant no longer accepts this sign-in: it was removed there, or it expired. Sign in again on the Connections page.
